liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Jack Straw** (2 reviews): Reviewer's first show, at age 14, opened with Jack Straw into Franklin's Tower; it changed their life; Reviewer hears the build as not the smoothest but train-powered, with an easy segue into Franklin's [21][24]
- **Brokedown Palace** (2 reviews): Closing Brokedown deeply moved the reviewer, who had attended all three nights of this run; Reviewer singles out the Brokedown Palace ending as a highlight [17][21]
- **Franklin's Tower** (1 review): Reviewer finds it breezy and potent but too short, missing an intro solo from Garcia [24]
- **Mama Tried** (1 other source): Uploader calls Garcia's first-set playing frenetic, naming Jack Straw, Franklin's Tower, Mama Tried and Big River [7]

## Setlist highlights

- **WMMR Wrapup**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [28]

## The recordings

- **gd1987-03-31.172773.ultramatrix.remaster.miksis.miller.flac16** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 22 songs; 160 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [1]
- **gd1987-03-31.169160.Philadelphia.PA.fm.wmmr.pearson.miller.t-flac1648**: FM broadcast; 21 songs; 161 min [2]
- **gd1987-03-31.139806.UltraMatrix.cm.miller.flac1644**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 21 songs; 152 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [4]
- **gd87-03-31.fm.miller.21267.sbeok.shnf**: FM broadcast; 21 songs; 148 min; rated 4.24/5 by 28 [6]. Said about its sound: Reviewer, who attended, expects the FM broadcast to sound better than the audience recording; Reviewer calls the broadcast's sound very good [19][26]

## Around the show

- Stage talk about: WMMR Tuning [1]
- Reviewer's first solo Dead show, on the floor; reserved-looking guys nearby turned into dancing Heads when lights went out [17]
- Reviewer thinks the band played this show with the radio audience in mind [18]
- Spectrum was about 30 minutes from the reviewer's home; a friend's spare ticket brought them along [21]
- Reviewer enjoys the radio promos between songs as fitting for the broadcast [24]
- WMMR Philadelphia DJ 'Bubba' John Stevens provides the commentary on the FM broadcast [26]
- Includes all circulating DJ banter, with extra banter from a second FM source at the start of set 2 [1]
- Reviewer finds the second set somewhat sleepier than the sparkling first set [16]
- Reviewer rates it a good show but not among the band's best [18]
- Reviewer says a similar killer version of the second song was played on 9-9-87 in Providence [20]
- Reviewer calls spring 1987 underrated, comparing this show favorably to the stunning Hartford 3/26 show [22]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1987-03-31.172773.ultramatrix.remaster.miksis.miller.flac16**: transferred by Remastered by Brian Miksis April 2025; source: Ultra Matrix SBD > Cassette Master (TDK MA-R90) > (Nakamichi CR-7A) > Tascam DA-3000 (DSF 1-bit/5.8 MHz) > KORG AudioGate 4 > Adobe Audition CC 2015 >… [1]. Also: Remastered and re-patched mix for the WMMR broadcast, using Miller/Pearson Ultramatrix and FM sources plus a Big River tape-flip patch [1]
- **gd1987-03-31.169160.Philadelphia.PA.fm.wmmr.pearson.miller.t-flac1648**: taped by Recorded by Don Pearson from inside The Spectrum; transferred by All Transfers and Mastering by Charlie Miller  October 2, 2024; source: FM (WMMR-FM) > Cassette Master (TDK SA-X90) [2]
- **gd1987-03-31.139806.UltraMatrix.cm.miller.flac1644**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: Ultra Matrix SBD > Cassette Master (TDK MA-R90) [4]. Also: Ultramatrix mix combining two sets of masters to make the show complete [4]
- **gd87-03-31.fm.miller.21267.sbeok.shnf**: source: Recording Info:FM -> Cassette Master -> DatTransfer Info:Dat -> Behringer UltraMatch SRC2000 -> CD (Tascam CDRW700) -> EAC -> SHNAll Transfers Done By Charlie… [6]
